reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 3 introduces core methodologies for tracking ball and player movements in multi-view environments. It begins with temporal hysteresis-based classification of ball candidates, leveraging likelihood thresholds to stabilize decisions over time. This approach mitigates transient errors during occlusions or visual ambiguities. The paper then details how multi-view tracking integrates heterogeneous sensor inputs—specifically, ground-plane projections from multiple cameras—to enhance positional accuracy. Using a Kalman-like update mechanism, it fuses these measurements into coherent player trajectories while maintaining uncertainty bounds. For ball trajectory reconstruction, the method models the ball's 3D path as a geometric median of multiple 3D lines derived from 2D projections. This allows for robust estimation even under partial visibility. Finally, the tracking-back mechanism resolves ambiguities by revisiting earlier frames and reclassifying merged tracks based on temporal consistency. These primitives collectively support high-fidelity spatiotemporal modeling essential for intelligent sports analytics.
